title: Hundreds, Tens and Ones
bigQuestion: How can three little digits stand for a number as big as 1,000?

story.title: The Button Jar
story.kicker: A big jar of buttons sits on a shelf. Nobody knows how many are inside.
paragraphs: Mrs. Diaz keeps a big glass jar on the shelf. It is full of buttons. Red ones, blue ones, tiny white ones. One day she asks the class a question. How many buttons are in the jar? Everyone guesses. Ten! A hundred! A million!

Two friends, Kai and Rosa, pour the buttons out. Kai starts to count. One, two, three. At forty-two, someone sneezes. Kai loses his place. He has to start again. Rosa has an idea. Let's make groups of ten, she says.

They make piles of ten buttons. Ten piles of ten make one hundred. They put each hundred in a paper cup. Soon the table is covered with cups. They stop and count the cups. Ten cups. That is ten hundreds. Ten hundreds make one thousand!

Mrs. Diaz smiles. You did not count 1,000 buttons one by one, she says. You counted hundreds, tens and ones. That is how big numbers work. Every big number is just groups. Groups of one hundred, groups of ten and some left over.
story.think: Why did making groups of ten help Kai and Rosa count faster than counting one by one?

lessons.title: Hundreds, Tens and Ones
lessons.mainIdea: A three-digit number is made of hundreds, tens and ones.
reading: Think of base-ten blocks. A little cube is one. A rod of ten cubes is a *ten*. A flat square of ten rods is a *hundred*. A hundred has 100 little cubes in it.
Look at 347. The 3 is in the hundreds place. It means 3 hundreds, or 300. The 4 is in the tens place. It means 4 tens, or 40. The 7 is in the ones place. It means 7 ones.
The place tells you the value. A 3 in the hundreds place is 300. A 3 in the ones place is just 3. Same digit, different job. Always ask: which place is it in?

words.d: a group of ten tens, or 100 ones
the spot a digit sits in, which tells its value

look.title: Blocks on the Table
look.text: Picture 2 flat hundreds on the table. Next to them are 5 rods of ten. Next to the rods are 6 little cubes. Count the hundreds. Count the tens. Count the ones. Say the number the blocks show.
look.prompt: What number do the blocks show? Say how many hundreds, tens and ones.

check.q: In 582, what does the 5 stand for?
check.why: The 5 is in the hundreds place. It means 5 hundreds, or 500.

check.q: How many tens make one hundred?
check.why: Ten rods of ten make one flat hundred. 10 tens = 100.

check.q: Which number has 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 9 ones?
check.why: 4 hundreds is 400. 0 tens is 0. 9 ones is 9. 400 + 0 + 9 = 409.

lessons.title: Expanded Form
lessons.mainIdea: Expanded form breaks a number into hundreds plus tens plus ones.
reading: You can stretch a number out. This is called *expanded form*. Take 347. It has 3 hundreds, 4 tens and 7 ones. So 347 = 300 + 40 + 7.
Try 615. The 6 means 600. The 1 means 10. The 5 means 5. Write it as 600 + 10 + 5. Add it back up. 600 + 10 = 610. Then 610 + 5 = 615. It matches.
Watch out for zeros. In 508, the 0 means 0 tens. So 508 = 500 + 8. Some students write 500 + 0 + 8. That is fine too. Just do not write 58!

words.d: a number written as hundreds plus tens plus ones, like 300 + 40 + 7

look.title: Stretch It Out
look.text: Rosa has 263 buttons. She puts 2 hundreds in cups. She puts 6 tens in rows. She keeps 3 loose. Write the cups, the rows and the loose buttons as an adding sentence.

check.why: 7 hundreds is 700. 2 tens is 20. 9 ones is 9. So 700 + 20 + 9.
306 has 3 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones. So 300 + 6.

lessons.title: Reading and Writing Numbers
lessons.mainIdea: Say the hundreds, then the tens and ones, to read a number up to 1,000.
reading: To read 347, say the hundreds first. Three hundred. Then say the rest like a two-digit number. Forty-seven. Three hundred forty-seven. Do not say 'and' in the middle.
Now write a number from words. Five hundred twelve. Five hundred is 500. Twelve is 12. Put them together: 512. Be careful with 'twelve'. It is one ten and two ones.
One *thousand* is written 1,000. It is ten hundreds. The comma helps your eye. Nine hundred ninety-nine is 999. One more makes 1,000.

words.d: one of the symbols 0 to 9 used to write numbers

look.title: Numbers in Words
look.cite: Number names and the digits that write them
look.prompt: Which number in the table has a 0 in the tens place? Which have a 0 in the ones place?

check.q: How do you write six hundred forty-two?
check.why: Six hundred is 600. Forty-two is 42. 600 + 42 = 642.
The 8 is 800. Then 0 tens and 3 ones. Eight hundred three.
999 + 1 = 1,000. Ten hundreds make one thousand.

lessons.title: Which Number Is Bigger?
lessons.mainIdea: Compare the hundreds first, then the tens, then the ones.
reading: Kai has 348 buttons. Rosa has 352. Who has more? Let's *compare*. Look at the hundreds first. Both have 3 hundreds. It is a tie. Move to the tens.
Kai has 4 tens. Rosa has 5 tens. 5 tens is more than 4 tens. So 352 is bigger than 348. You do not even need the ones. The tens settled it.
A common mistake is to look at the ones first. 348 has an 8. 352 has a 2. But 8 ones is only 8. One ten is worth 10. Bigger places win. Start on the left.

words.d: to look at two numbers and tell which is bigger, smaller or the same

look.title: Two Towers
look.text: Look at two towers of blocks. Tower A has 5 hundreds and 1 ten. Tower B has 4 hundreds, 9 tens and 9 ones. Tower B looks busy with all those blocks. But count the hundreds. Which tower is really worth more?
look.prompt: Which tower is worth more, and what place did you check to decide?

check.why: Both have 4 hundreds. 8 tens is more than 7 tens. 481 is bigger.
209 has 2 hundreds. 190 has only 1 hundred. 190 is smaller.

check.q: To compare 635 and 638, which place do you need to check last?
check.why: The hundreds tie at 6. The tens tie at 3. The ones decide it. 8 is more than 5, so 638 is bigger.

lessons.title: The Signs >, < and =
lessons.mainIdea: Use > for greater than, < for less than and = for equal to.
reading: Three signs help you compare. The sign > means *greater than*. The sign < means *less than*. The sign = means *equal to*. The open side of > or < always faces the bigger number.
Compare 352 and 348. 352 is greater. Write 352 > 348. Now flip it. 348 is less than 352. Write 348 < 352. Both say the same thing.
What about 500 and 500? They are the same. Write 500 = 500. Think of the sign as a hungry mouth. It opens to eat the bigger number.

words.d: the same amount; the sign is =

look.title: Feed the Mouth
look.text: Kai writes 720 ? 702. He is not sure which sign goes in the middle. Both have 7 hundreds. Look at the tens. 720 has 2 tens. 702 has 0 tens. Which number is bigger? Which way should the mouth open?
look.prompt: Which sign belongs in 720 ? 702: greater than, less than or equal to?

check.why: The hundreds tie. 1 ten is less than 5 tens. So 415 < 451.
The sign > means greater than. 9 tens beats 0 tens, so 890 is greater.
300 + 40 is 340. So 340 = 340. They are equal.

lessons.title: Counting by 5s, 10s and 100s
lessons.mainIdea: Skip counting adds the same amount each time: 5, 10 or 100.
reading: To *skip count* means to count by jumps. Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. Count by 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. Count by 100s: 100, 200, 300, 400, 500.
You can start anywhere. Start at 340 and count by 10s. 340, 350, 360, 370. Only the tens digit changes. Start at 340 and count by 100s. 340, 440, 540. Only the hundreds digit changes.
Skip counting is fast. Rosa has 6 cups of 100 buttons. She counts 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600. Six jumps of 100 is 600. Much faster than counting one by one.

words.d: to count by jumps of the same size, like 5, 10, 15, 20

look.title: Counting Cups of 100
look.cite: Rosa's button cups, 100 buttons in each cup
look.prompt: How many buttons would 7 cups hold? Keep the pattern going.

check.why: 45 + 5 = 50. Each jump adds 5.

check.q: Count by 10s from 570: 570, 580, ___. What comes next?
check.why: 580 + 10 = 590. Only the tens digit changes.
450 + 100 = 550. The hundreds digit goes up by 1.

lessons.title: 100 More and 100 Less
lessons.mainIdea: Adding or taking away 100 changes only the hundreds digit.
reading: What is 100 *more* than 462? Add one hundred. The hundreds digit goes from 4 to 5. The tens and ones stay the same. 462 + 100 = 562.
What is 100 *less* than 462? Take one hundred away. The hundreds digit goes from 4 to 3. 462 − 100 = 362. The 6 and the 2 do not move.
The same trick works for 10. 10 more than 462 is 472. 10 less than 462 is 452. Only the tens digit changes. Be careful near 9 tens: 10 more than 495 is 505.

words.d: a bigger amount; 100 more means add 100
a smaller amount; 100 less means take away 100

look.title: The Elevator Game
look.text: Pretend a tall building has floors numbered like our numbers. You are on floor 384. The up button takes you up 100 floors. The down button takes you down 100 floors. Press up once. Where are you? Now start again at 384 and press down twice.
look.prompt: What floor is 100 more than 384? What floor is 200 less than 384?

check.why: 738 + 100 = 838. Only the hundreds digit changes, from 7 to 8.
520 − 100 = 420. The hundreds digit drops from 5 to 4.
293 + 10 = 303. 9 tens plus 1 ten is 10 tens, which makes a new hundred.

lessons.title: Even and Odd Numbers
lessons.mainIdea: Even numbers make pairs with none left over; odd numbers have one left over.
reading: Put 8 buttons in pairs. You get 4 pairs. None are left over. So 8 is *even*. Put 7 buttons in pairs. You get 3 pairs and 1 left over. So 7 is *odd*.
Here is a fast check. Look at the ones digit only. If it is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8, the number is even. If it is 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9, the number is odd. So 346 is even. 231 is odd.
Even numbers are doubles. 8 is 4 + 4. 10 is 5 + 5. 12 is 6 + 6. Odd numbers cannot split into two equal groups. Try to split 9 in half. You get 4 and 5, not a match.

words.d: a number that makes pairs with none left over, like 2, 4, 6
a number that leaves one out when you make pairs, like 1, 3, 5

look.title: Partners for the Game
look.text: Kai's class has 23 students. The teacher says: find a partner! Everyone pairs up. Picture the pairs standing in a row. Does someone stand alone? Now picture a class of 24. Does anyone stand alone this time?
look.prompt: Is 23 even or odd? Is 24 even or odd? How do you know?

check.why: 18 ends in 8. It makes 9 pairs with none left over. 18 is even.
31 ends in 1. Pairs leave one out. 31 is odd.

check.q: Which number is a double, like 6 = 3 + 3?
check.why: 14 = 7 + 7. It is even. 9 and 11 cannot be split into two equal groups.

review.q: What number is 5 hundreds, 7 tens and 3 ones?

review.why: 8 hundreds is 800. 4 tens is 40. There are 0 ones. So 800 + 40.
907 − 100 = 807. The hundreds digit drops from 9 to 8.
489 ends in 9, so it is odd. Numbers that end in 0 or 4 are even.
